answer.text: Not necessarily straight away: a motorcycle that is used very rarely, with the battery terminals still connected, is bound to lose its battery charge and can end up with a dead battery.
The basic starting step is to turn the ignition key to ON and put the engine kill switch on the right-hand handlebar in the run position.

watchouts.text: For a motorcycle not used for a month or more, the manual says storage precautions should be taken, and for re-use after storage it is preferable to have the motorcycle prepared at a Royal Enfield Authorised Service Centre.
If the battery was disconnected and removed for storage, check that its voltage is within specification before refitting it; if not, recharge it at an authorised service workshop or battery dealer.
When reconnecting the battery, connect the red (+ve) terminal first and then the black (-ve) terminal.
If the engine does not start, do not hold the starter switch down for long periods, as this drains the battery below the 10 V threshold; have it checked at a Royal Enfield Authorised Service Centre.
Do not press the starter button for more than 5 seconds after three successive crankings; wait 15 to 20 seconds for the battery to recover.

disclaimers.text: The manual gives no complete post-storage restart checklist, so this answer is partial.
The manual does not say whether an unprepared bike stored for over a month can simply be restarted, and it cannot know what storage preparation you did.
